pronunciation.notes: Gern and gerne mean the same. Gerne is a little softer and very common in speech.

word.meaning: gladly; used to say you like doing something
word.shortDefinition: Add it to any verb to say you enjoy doing it.

intro.title: The easiest way to say 'I like'
paragraphs: German doesn't need a special verb to say you like doing something. You just do the thing, gladly: Ich schwimme gern. I swim gladly, I like swimming.
Gern is one of the most useful words at A1. It turns every verb you know into a preference, and it's also how Germans say 'you're welcome'.

etymology.title: Where it comes from
etymology.summary: Gern comes from an old Germanic word meaning eager or desiring. English kept the same root in the verb 'yearn'.

cognates.note: to desire, from the same root

tables.title: Like, prefer, like most
tables.intro: Gern has irregular comparative forms, which you'll use all the time.
notes: Never gerner. The comparative is lieber, from the same root as lieb (dear).

keyTrap.title: The big trap: word order
keyTrap.explanation: Gern is an adverb, not a verb, so the real verb still has to take second place. Gern comes after it.

wrong.verdict: The verb has to come second.

correct.note: In a question the verb comes first.

commonMistakes.title: gern for doing, mögen for things
commonMistakes.explanation: Use gern with a verb. With a noun, mögen is more natural.
commonMistakes.correct: Ich mag Pizza. / Ich esse gern Pizza.

commonMistakes.title: The comparative
commonMistakes.explanation: It's irregular, so there's no gerner.

commonMistakes.title: Ordering
commonMistakes.explanation: Ich hätte gern … is the polite way to ask for something in a shop or café.

sampleSentences.german: Ich koche gern, aber ich spüle nicht gern.
sampleSentences.english: I like cooking, but I don't like washing up.

sampleSentences.german: Was machst du gern am Wochenende?
sampleSentences.english: What do you like doing at the weekend?

sampleSentences.german: Ich fahre lieber mit dem Zug.

quiz.explanation: The verb comes second, gern follows it.

quiz.prompt: Tee oder Kaffee? Ich trinke ___ Tee. (prefer)
Someone says Danke! What do you answer?

quiz.explanation: The verb comes second, gern after it.

quiz.prompt: Am ___ esse ich Pizza. (most of all)

memoryHook: Gern = gladly. Do the thing, then add gern: Ich tanze gern. Better is lieber, best is am liebsten.
